- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or shows recent reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 3–7 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 1–3% per day.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical 30-day average if deviation >3σ.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price in early periods (e.g., 1–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2–0.4), model tends to err on the side of overconfidence; reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect lower conviction.
